rationale: Review the current fixed input, actual correlated recurrence observation and the source-backed closure argument as one checker correspondence assessment.

review_items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact 5ca4018032bc415e95df5b07310fd84d v1, its saved harness/plan and CheckRun aaa140bb2be04782910221a321e75432 against C-auto-exit-continuation v1. The actual monitor result has no parsing errors and correlates result index 10 with operation index 8 and suffix-start index 9, all operation_id aborted_transfer/implicit-remove-3. I reconstructed the Go test Output chunks per test into complete lines (large JSON events are split by go test -json), decoded both saved state trees and independently confirmed they are equal. The initial failed attempt to parse each Output chunk separately was a local inspection error, not missing evidence or a target/tool execution failure.

Applicability and responsibility: S-jointcontract and S-autoleave-tracker-contract assign automatic exit to Raft for implicit mode, contrasting explicit mode with application-proposed exit. The entering operation already committed and applied; the caller has completed required work. S-autoleave specifically implements the internal proposal and anticipates transfer rejection/retry. External Propose retry duties do not require an unrelated command to complete this already applied automatic transition. No numerical deadline is inferred.

Actual legal history: three real bootstrapped RawNodes elect node 1 in term 2; its empty entry commits/applies at 4. A real implicit removal of voter 3 commits at 5, yielding incoming {1,2}, outgoing {1,2,3}, AutoLeave=true. The driver invokes public ApplyConfChange and then public TransferLeader(2) before the same Ready's Advance. Node's event loop permits handling messages while Ready is outstanding; RawNode calls here remain serialized. Every batch appends entries and writes HardState before any message delivery, applies each committed entry in order, then advances once. Only the first generated TimeoutNow is lost; every later message is serviced. MemoryStorage substitutes completed persistence only in a no-crash run; it is not claimed to test physical disk durability. No forged response, injected term/log state, target mutation or premature application supplies the witness.

Observations: after the transfer prefix, node 1's applied/commit/last are 5, transfer=2, no leave entry exists. At tick 20 the transfer has aborted, leader/term remain 1/2, both configurations still contain a viable quorum, all work is drained, and index 5 is applied at all nodes. Between ticks 20 and 30 the recorded suffix delivers 20 MsgHeartbeat and 20 MsgHeartbeatResp messages, no other message types. At tick 30 the complete recorded protocol state repeats, pending=true, transfer=0, applied=commit=last=5, and every queue/Ready completion is drained. The predicate cycle_repeat implies not pending is therefore false for the fully correlated witness. Test process success is merely successful collection, not the property verdict.

Recurrence coverage and induction: the observer recursively reads all RawNode fields and reachable raft/log/tracker/MemoryStorage fields, including election and heartbeat timers, randomized timeout values, progress/inflight accounting, current callbacks, votes, read queues, pending configuration index, unstable offsets/snapshots, HardState, stable entries, application bookkeeping, and stepsOnAdvance. It also records the network queue, caller application journals and already-used one-packet-loss policy. At both boundaries all three nodes have applied=applying=commit=5, no unstable entries/snapshot, offset=offsetInProgress=6, zero outstanding application bytes and empty stepsOnAdvance. The leader tracks all peers at Match=5 in replicate state with zero inflights. Logger objects and increment-only MemoryStorage.callStats are excluded; source search shows these counters never determine behavior. traceLogger is nil and the runner has no with_tla tag. Mutex state is captured. Function code identity omits closure representation, but the only tick closures bind the same live raft receiver, and this suffix does not replace them. Pointer addresses and slice backing slots beyond length are not claimed as byte-for-byte heap equality; no suffix branch relies on them, and stored messages/entries are immutable here. The observer allocates independent scalar/container trees, so later target mutations cannot silently rewrite the left observation.

The repeated input is ten identical Tick-all/fully-drain rounds. Each follower receives a heartbeat every round and resets electionElapsed, remaining below its captured election threshold; the leader sees live joint quorum and cycles its counters. Heartbeat replies mark activity but, with matched replicas and no read context, neither append new entries nor schedule application. Message-only Ready/Advance has no storage/apply completion callback once unstable/application work is empty (S-apply-response-trigger, S-advance). No snapshot or external asynchronous worker exists. The only randomness source is called on timeout reset, which this stable-role suffix never reaches. Thus the equal protocol state plus these read transition branches admits repetition with live messaging and no automatic leave, instead of extrapolating from finite waiting or equal business fields alone.

Controls and scope: the no-transfer branch actually appends/applies leave at 6 before the observation window. Its full-state recurrence is false because removed node 3's election counter advances; its implication hold is not evidence of a general liveness proof. In the transfer branch a later normal proposal is admitted and committed, producing a new application callback and automatic leave at 7, so the result does not allege inability to make ordinary log progress. Existing leadership-loss recovery test similarly uses a new election and applied work. These recovery paths bound the finding; they do not supply an event that the caller owes in the stationary suffix. The supported cause is the rejected internal proposal with no retry at abort/heartbeat/message-only Advance. Wider availability consequences and other storage modes remain unmeasured. No correspondence issue found for this scoped witness; this is a semantic review, not an independent execution or universal proof.
limitations: The fixed witness uses synchronous RawNode/Ready, three initial voters and one implicit removal; no claim about every membership or storage mode.
No crash-durability, consensus-safety, numeric deadline, client endpoint or whole-cluster availability result.
Recurrence is semantic protocol-state equality under the declared live suffix, not equality of the entire Go heap or test-process counters.
The no-transfer control is a contrast, not an additional applicable aborted-transfer operation.
review_items.report_title: 领导权转移失败后，自动退出联合配置失去继续触发
review_items.report_answer: 固定执行中，隐式联合配置已提交并应用，丢失一条 TimeoutNow 后原领导者继续服务；在持续心跳和完整处理待办工作的十个 tick 周期内，协议状态完整重复而 AutoLeave 仍未完成。无转移对照正常退出，后续普通提案也能恢复退出，因此结论限于缺少无关新提案时的自动继续机制，不是共识安全或整体服务停顿。

feedback.answered: The fixed execution observes a repeatable live suffix after transfer abort: tick-20 and tick-30 full protocol states compare equal, with AutoLeave=true and no leave entry, while 20 heartbeats and 20 replies are delivered and all work drains. Source transition analysis excludes entropy, deferred storage/application callbacks and hidden retry triggers in that suffix. The no-transfer control and later-proposal rescue succeed. This answers the scoped lost-continuation question; the measured violation is submitted for correspondence assessment rather than inferred from test success.
remaining: Unmeasured consequence: whether a particular later failure pattern would make retained outgoing membership reduce service availability.
Other independent map surfaces, including read continuation and storage ownership, remain open.
feedback.rationale: The current execution supplies the missing full-state recurrence; recovery controls narrow the cause and consequence instead of suppressing contrary evidence.
